author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
review: 'The Great Gatsby' by F. Scott Fitzgerald is a timeless masterpiece that delves into the decadence and disillusionment of the Jazz Age. Set in the Roaring Twenties, the novel unveils the enigmatic Jay Gatsby's extravagant parties, masking a pursuit of lost love. Narrated by Nick Carraway, the story explores themes of wealth, love, and the American Dream, drawing readers into a vivid portrayal of the glittering yet elusive world of the East and West Egg. Fitzgerald's prose is both poetic and haunting, weaving a compelling narrative that transcends its era. A poignant exploration of societal excess and the human condition, 'The Great Gatsby' remains a literary gem that resonates across generations.

author: Harper Lee
review: Scout Finch grows up in a small Alabama town where her father, Atticus, defends a Black man accused of a crime. The trial and her fascination with a reclusive neighbor expose the town’s prejudices and test her understanding of courage.

author: George Orwell
review: Winston Smith rewrites history for the ruling Party in a society of constant surveillance. His private doubts and a forbidden relationship with Julia put him at odds with a regime determined to control both public life and private thought.

author: J.D. Salinger
review: After being expelled from school, teenager Holden Caulfield spends several days wandering New York City. His sardonic narration reveals his loneliness, his grief, and his fear of growing up.

author: Jane Austen
review: Elizabeth Bennet initially dismisses the wealthy Mr. Darcy as proud and disagreeable. As their paths keep crossing, both must reconsider their first impressions in a story about marriage, class, and family expectations.

author: J.R.R. Tolkien
review: Bilbo Baggins leaves his comfortable home to accompany a company of dwarves on a quest to reclaim their mountain kingdom from the dragon Smaug. Along the way, he discovers a talent for getting himself and his companions out of trouble.

bookName: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
author: J.K. Rowling
review: On his eleventh birthday, Harry learns he is a wizard and begins school at Hogwarts. As he makes friends and discovers his family’s past, he and his classmates stumble upon a secret hidden inside the castle.

author: Paulo Coelho
review: A young Andalusian shepherd named Santiago sets out for Egypt after dreaming of a treasure near the pyramids. Along the way, he meets people who challenge how he thinks about ambition, loss, and the choices that shape a life.

author: Paula Hawkins
review: Rachel watches the same houses from her train each day and imagines the lives of the people inside. When a woman she has been watching disappears, Rachel becomes entangled in the investigation and has to reckon with gaps in her own memory.
